title: PR risk ladder & rollback scratchpad - Mina Park
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for shaping a lightweight PR risk ladder and rollback playbook for small-to-medium changes in serving-runtime. This is messy, unfinished. Notes to self + checklist to iterate into a sharable runbook.

High-level goals:
- Make rollbacks predictable and fast (<=5–10m manual action for high-severity regressions).
- Surface the right signals to avoid noisy rollbacks.
- Give on-call and reviewers a clear path: detect -> assess -> rollback -> restore.

Risk ladder (idea):
1) Low: non-critical refactor, no config change, tests pass, no perf impact. Actions: basic smoke, merge on green.
2) Medium: touches request path or batching logic, potential latency regression. Actions: run perf microbench locally, canary to 5% traffic, monitor latency+errors for 30m.
3) High: changes cache/KV handling, model routing, or kernel selection heuristics. Actions: gated canary + manual approval, automated rollback if error rate > X or 95th p50 regressed > Y% for 10m.
4) Critical: migrating data format, changing KV semantics, or global config toggles. Actions: feature flag, staged rollout with manual sign-off at each stage, rollback pre-wired.

Quick signal set (first-pass):
- 5xx rate (per-route) delta > 50% over baseline (5m window).
- P95 latency increase > 30% over baseline (5m)
- Model token generation stalls / increase in token timeouts
- Increase in queue length / backlog metric (serving_runtime.request_queue_length)
- Error budget burn (SLO dashboard alert)
- CI flaky test failure patterns (new failures vs. historical)

Automated rollback thresholds (examples for canary):
- If 5xx_rate_canary > 3x control AND absolute 5xx_rate_canary > 0.5% for 5m -> auto-rollback
- If p95_canary / p95_control > 1.35 for 10m -> roll back and notify
- If queue_length growth > 2x baseline for 5m -> roll back

Manual assessment checklist (what to look for before flipping rollback):
- Is the increased error rate on a single route or system-wide? (route-level vs infra-level)
- Are there alerts from infra (OOMs, GPU errors)? Look at node-exporter, nvidia-smi logs.
- Any recent infra deploys overlapping? (coord with release-engineering)
- Can the failing requests be isolated by headers/tenant? If yes, throttle that tenant instead.
- Are telemetry labels consistent? e.g., model version, kernel tag, host pool.

Rollback primitives (ops commands & quick steps):
- Revert to previous model variant: infra CLI -> reroute --from canary --to control --weight 0. Set in routing policy.
- Pull old image on dedicated pool: kubectl -n redwood set image deployment/serving-runtime serving-runtime=redwood/serving-runtime:<previous-tag>
- Disable feature flag: ffctl disable <flag> --env=prod
- Short-circuit routing: add temporary route to fallback model variant with strict timeouts
- Scale-up control pool if rollback causes resource pressure: k scale deploy control-pool --replicas N

Smoke tests to run immediately post-rollback (scriptable):
- curl /health and /metrics for 30s -> expect no 5xx
- run integration prompt test: small prompt -> expect completion under SLO
- run embedding test on small payload (100 vectors) -> success
- check KV cache hitrate metrics (no large drop)

Notes on alerts and noise:
- Avoid auto-rollback for noisy downstream errors (e.g., storage blips). Add filter: only rollback if error traces include serving-runtime stack frames or grpc statuses INTERNAL/UNAVAILABLE from our process.
- Use anomaly detection baseline windows: rolling 24h for p95 baseline, shorter windows for spikes.

Testing checklist to reduce false positives pre-merge:
- Local perf harness with at least 10k tokens across varying seq lengths
- Synthetic canary run in staging that mimics production distribution (sampled tenants)
- Add minimal observability tags to new code paths: {deploy_id, pr_number, feature_flag} in logs

Operational ergonomics: who presses rollback?
- On-call SRE -> auto-rollback triggers + notifies on-call.
- If manual rollback needed: owning engineer (PR author) or release-engineer must acknowledge -> then SRE executes.
- Post-rollback postmortem planned within 48h.

Open TODOs / unresolved: (notes to self)
- Define exact numeric thresholds with product/console (Rhea). Current numbers are placeholders (X, Y).
- Add runbook snippets to ops-runbooks repo; link CI job that can test rollback flow in staging.
- Make small CLI tool to compute delta metrics for canary vs control (PromQL templated queries).
- Discuss whether we should allow per-PR opt-out if a change is low-risk (ff guard?).
- Capture example PromQLs here before moving to Confluence.

Example PromQLs (starter):
- 5xx rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..", route=~"<route>"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route=~"<route>"}[5m]))
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"<route>"}[5m])) by (le))

Mental model for canary sizing:
- Prefer multiple short canaries (5% for 15m x 3) over single long canary. Faster detection + easier rollback.
- For critical changes use smaller steps: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with manual ack at each stage.

Notes on communication:
- If rolling back, automatically ping: #prod-deploys, #oncall, PR author, and affected-sigs channels. Template message: who rolled back, why, metrics links, next steps.

Post-rollback checklist for author:
- Run local repro script and attach failing trace to PR
- Open follow-up PR with fix and explicit test coverage for telemetry gap that missed signal
- Schedule quick sync with SRE within 24h to align on postmortem and prevent recurrence

Final small todos for this doc:
- Convert to formal runbook + add playbook snippets for common rollback commands (Jonas to review).
- Add example canary dashboard json and Prometheus alerts to infra repo.
- Clean up thresholds after two weeks of collection.

Random friction notes (personal):
- I keep tripping over flaky CI for perf tests; need a lightweight harness that runs locally with docker.
- Consider a tiny synthetic workload generator that can be run as part of PR checks (non-blocking) but produces a perf-report artifact.

End-of-scratchpad. This needs iteration — convert to proper template before sharing widely.
